meta.scope: Commonly-used Lumerical script API subset — NOT exhaustive. If a function is not listed here, do NOT assume its signature; call reference_lookup(list_only=true) or check Lumerical documentation.
meta.note: Each entry's verified_against should be updated to the Lumerical version (e.g. '241') after live verification. Mark 'pending' until then.

getresult.returns: dataset object — fields accessed with .f, .lambda, .Ex, .Ey, .Ez, .Hx, .Hy, .Hz, .x, .y, .z, .T, .R, .P, .power depending on monitor type

valid_args.name: monitor name (e.g. 'DFT', 'index') or 'FDTD' for global results
valid_args.property: dataset name, e.g. 'E', 'H', 'T', 'P', 'index' — must match monitor output flags

common_pitfalls: getresult returns a dataset object, not a scalar — use .field access (via getv) to get arrays
Second arg specifies which dataset within the monitor's results; with one arg it returns a list of available datasets

getdata.returns: array of field values (not a dataset object — direct array)
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202 (2026-11): the command exists; in layout mode it reports "the d-card named ... was not found" and tells you to run first
getdata returns a raw array, not a dataset — preferred when you want just one field
getresult + getv(dataset.field) is equivalent but returns the whole dataset

getnamed.returns: property value (type depends on property: float, string, array)
common_pitfalls: Property names have spaces (e.g. 'x span', 'wavelength start') — use exact casing
getnamed only works for scalar/string properties; for datasets use getresult
Confirmed working for all 35+ properties in get_scene_info
getnamed.verified_against: proven — used extensively in get_scene_info and get_parameters

valid_args.value: new value — number, string, or array

common_pitfalls: Does NOT work for script properties — use set() with 'setup script'/'analysis script' instead
Property names are case-sensitive and may contain spaces

valid_args.value: new value (string for scripts, number for properties)

common_pitfalls: set() operates on the currently selected object (select() first)
For script content, always use the set_script tool instead of execute('set("setup script",...)')
For non-script properties, use setnamed() which does NOT require select()

addfdtd.returns: none (creates FDTD solver region in new project)
common_pitfalls: Only needed for new blank projects (new tool calls this automatically)
Configure FDTD region via setnamed('FDTD', prop, val) after creation

addrect.returns: none (creates a rectangle structure object, auto-named)
common_pitfalls: Auto-generates a name like 'rectangle_1' — capture it via select() + getnamed('name') after creation
Configure via setnamed or set_parameter tool after creation

addcircle.returns: none (creates a circle/cylinder structure object, auto-named)
common_pitfalls: Same pattern as addrect — auto-named, configure after creation

addtfsf.returns: none (creates a TFSF plane wave source, auto-named)
common_pitfalls: Creates a total-field/scattered-field source — auto-named like 'TFSF_1'
Configure direction, wavelength range, injection axis via setnamed after creation

addgaussian.returns: none (creates a Gaussian beam source, auto-named)
common_pitfalls: Auto-named like 'gaussian_1'
For dipole sources use adddipole(), for plane waves use addplane()

addplane.returns: none (creates a plane wave source, auto-named)
common_pitfalls: Auto-named like 'plane_1'
May not exist in all Lumerical versions — use addtfsf if addplane is unavailable
Auto-named like 'dipole_1'
Set dipole type (Electric/Magnetic) and polarization angle after creation via setnamed
Auto-named like 'power_1'
Set monitor type (2D/3D/1D), output flags via setnamed after creation

addmesh.returns: none (creates a mesh override region, auto-named)
common_pitfalls: Auto-named like 'mesh_1'
Set dx/dy/dz via setnamed for mesh size override
Returns a generated name like 'material_1' — you MUST capture this return value
Built-in database materials (e.g. 'Au (Gold) - Johnson and Christy') need no addmaterial — just assign the name string via setnamed
After addmaterial, configure properties via setmaterial()
Property names vary by material model type — call getmaterial('name') without property to list available properties
nk data expects [wavelengths_array, n_array, k_array] in meters

getmaterial.returns: with property: property value; without property: list of available property names
common_pitfalls: Call getmaterial(name) WITHOUT property first to discover all settable property names

addvar.signature: NOT AVAILABLE in v202 — 'addvar is not a valid function or variable name'.
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202: addvar/addvarfdtd/setvar/getvar are all dead via LSF *and* appCall
Writing addvar into a script does not help — the command is gone in v202
Model variables are created with adduserprop("name", type_code, value) while ::model is SELECTED (see the adduserprop entry), or in the GUI
sweep parameter paths like ::model::gap require the variable to exist first — model_set(name="::model", properties={...}) creates it

setvar.signature: NOT AVAILABLE in v202 (same as addvar).
common_pitfalls: Dead on v202 — use getnamed/setnamed on existing properties instead

getvar.signature: NOT AVAILABLE in v202 (same as addvar).
common_pitfalls: Dead on v202 — use getnamed/getv on existing properties instead

adduserprop.signature: adduserprop("name", type_code, value)  — acts on the CURRENTLY SELECTED object
adduserprop.returns: none (declares a user property / model variable on that object)
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202: select the target first — select("mygroup") for a group property. With nothing (or a non-group) selected it fails with 'adduserprop requires a single structure or analysis group object to be selected'

The model root (::model, type 'ObjectModelRoot') ACCEPTS adduserprop, but a property created that way does NOT show up in the GUI's "Edit analysis group" dialog — that dialog lists ANALYSIS properties, so use addanalysisprop for ::model (the bridge does)
Structure groups are the intended target: adduserprop is what their Parameters table shows
The 2-arg form adduserprop('name', value) FAILS on v202
The string-type form adduserprop('name', value, 'Length') ALSO FAILS on v202 ('argument list ... command is incorrect') — the type must be the INTEGER code
An existing property is updated with setnamed(obj, name, value); adduserprop is only for creating a new one

NOT idempotent (verified live on v202): calling adduserprop again for a property that already exists does NOT error and does NOT update it — it creates a SUFFIXED CLONE (period -> period2 -> period3). A group setup script that re-declares its own properties therefore piles up clones every time runsetup runs, and bare-name references in that script silently point at a renamed property

Correct pattern for a re-runnable group script: declare the properties ONCE from outside (model_set(name="mygroup", properties={...}) — the bridge only calls adduserprop when setnamed failed), and let the script read them by bare name
addanalysisprop (analysis groups) has the same 3-arg/selection semantics and the same non-idempotency
Registering adduserprop in a setup script only takes effect when that script actually runs (runsetup) — it is NOT executed by writing the script alone

In an ANALYSIS group's own *setup* script, the group's properties are not usable as bare names on v202 (verified: the script fails with 'Failed to evaluate code' while the same script works on a structure group); write literals there and keep the properties in sync with model_set
adduserprop.verified_against: proven live on v202 — model root, structure group and analysis group

queryuserprop.signature: queryuserprop()  — no arguments, acts on the current selection (model root or structure group)
queryuserprop.returns: {'name': [...], 'type': ['0', '2', ...]} for the user properties of the selected object
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202: select("::model"); queryuserprop() lists GUI-created *and* adduserprop-created model variables — this is the reliable way to enumerate them (regex-scanning scripts is not)
On an analysis group it aborts with 'NULL pointer access' — use queryanalysisprop(obj) there
An empty object is returned when the selection has no user properties

addanalysisprop.signature: addanalysisprop("name", type_code, value)  — acts on the CURRENTLY SELECTED analysis group
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202: select("ag1"); addanalysisprop("period", 2, 1e-6) creates the property; the 2-arg and 4-arg (object-first) forms both fail with 'argument list for addanalysisprop command is incorrect'

**This is the command that fills the Analysis > Variables table** of the GUI's "Edit analysis group" dialog — for the MODEL ROOT too: select("::model"); addanalysisprop("gap", 2, 200e-9). A model property created with adduserprop instead does NOT appear in that dialog (verified in the GUI)
Structure groups are the other way round: they use adduserprop
Analysis and user properties SHARE a namespace: declaring a name that already exists creates a suffixed clone ("gap" -> "gap2") instead of updating it
Verify with select("<obj>"); queryanalysisprop("<obj>") — the query needs the object selected
addanalysisprop.verified_against: proven live on v202 (model root and analysis groups)

addanalysisresult.signature: addanalysisresult("name")  — ONE argument on the model root / analysis group
addanalysisresult.returns: none (declares a result name for the dialog's Results table)
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202: the 2-arg form addanalysisresult("name", value) and the 3-arg form both FAIL on the model root with 'Failed to evaluate code'; inside an analysis script the value-carrying form is what Lumerical's own templates use
Declare it with the object selected: select("::model"); addanalysisresult("T_spectrum")
Verify with select("<obj>"); queryanalysisresult("<obj>") -> ['T_spectrum', ...]

queryanalysisprop.signature: queryanalysisprop("objname") — the object must ALSO be selected
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202: with nothing (or an ordinary object) selected it fails with 'queryanalysisprop requires a single analysis group object to be selected' — call select("::model") first
This is the exact content of the GUI dialog's Analysis > Variables table
The model root counts: queryanalysisprop("::model") lists the model's parameters

queryanalysisresult.signature: queryanalysisresult("objname") — the object must ALSO be selected
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202; this is the content of the GUI dialog's Results table
Same selection requirement as queryanalysisprop

select.returns: none (selects an object, making it the target for subsequent operations)

valid_args.object_name: full path or relative name of an object

common_pitfalls: Many Lumerical functions (set, get, delete) operate on the CURRENTLY SELECTED object — call select() first
selectall() selects all objects in the current scope
groupscope('::model') resets to root scope before select()
delete() takes NO arguments — first call select('name') then delete()
The execute tool handles delete("name") automatically by wrapping select+delete
In Lumerical script LSF: delete; — no parentheses

valid_args.sweep_name: name of the parameter sweep (as defined in the Sweep editor)

common_pitfalls: Throws an error if the sweep has not been run yet — use get_sweep_info first
For individual monitor results within a sweep, access via getresult inside the sweep's analysis script

farfield.signature: NOT AVAILABLE in v202 — 'farfield is not a valid function or variable name'. Use farfield3d / farfieldpolar3d for far-field projection.
farfield.returns: none (performs far-field projection on selected monitor in analysis mode)
common_pitfalls: Must be called in analysis mode (switchtolayout first to go back, then run?)
farfieldfilter(α) sets the numerical aperture filter (α∈[0,1]) — α=0.8 is valid but filters at NA=0.8
Results accessed via farfield3d() / farfieldpolar() after farfield() call
Should be called after farfield() projection has been computed
Returns angular distribution data

farfieldpolar.signature: NOT AVAILABLE in v202 — 'farfieldpolar is not a valid function or variable name'. Use farfieldpolar2d / farfieldpolar3d instead.
farfieldpolar.returns: polar far-field data array (angle, amplitude, phase)
common_pitfalls: farfieldpolar3d exists — 3D polar data
farfieldpolar2d exists — 2D polar cross-section
Verified live on v202 (2026-11): the command exists; without monitor data it reports "no d-card ... with the necessary data"
Returns total transmission (T) through the monitor plane
For polarization-resolved transmission use getresult + field component

dipolepower.returns: total power emitted by a dipole source
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202 (2026-11): the command exists but returns an empty error string when the context is not suitable (this is documented in docs/verified/v202.md)
Returns the total radiated power — useful for normalizing Purcell factor calculations
Must be called in analysis mode with the dipole as an active source

haveresult.returns: 1 (true) or 0 (false) — whether the named result exists
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202 (2026-11): returns 1.0/0.0; it is true for objects that CAN hold results, so confirm with getresult before treating it as "data exists"
Use this BEFORE getresult to avoid errors when no results exist yet
Saves to Lumerical's working directory unless absolute path is given
For result datasets: matlabsave('out.mat', _br_d) after _br_d = getresult(...)

switchtolayout.returns: none (switches FDTD solver to layout mode)
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202 (2026-11): returns to layout mode; layoutmode() reports 1/0
After running a simulation you are in analysis mode — switchtolayout() returns to layout mode for editing

addvarfdtd.signature: NOT AVAILABLE in v202 — 'is not a valid function or variable name'.
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202 alongside addvar/setvar/getvar — the whole variable-command family is gone
Use adduserprop("name", type_code, value) with ::model selected

common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202: a DFT monitor is added with addpower(); its DFT/frequency-domain output is configured through the monitor's properties

findresult.signature: NOT AVAILABLE in v202 — 'is not a valid function or variable name'.
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202; haveresult(name) is the command that exists

hasresult.signature: NOT AVAILABLE in v202 — 'is not a valid function or variable name'.
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202 — use haveresult(name), which returns 1/0

addobject.signature: addobject("<catalog id>")  -> inserts an OBJECT LIBRARY item into the current project
addobject.returns: none (the item is copied in and its setup script re-runs)
common_pitfalls: Verified live on v202 (2026-09): addobject("Qanalysis") created Analysis Group "Qanalysis" with 4 time monitors t1..t4 and its setup/analysis scripts intact; addobject("ring_resonator") created Structure Group "ring resonator" with 8 child waveguides; addobject("sphere") created a plain Sphere (some library items are primitives, not groups)
The created object keeps the library item's own name, spaces included ("ring resonator")
The library lives at <LUMERICAL_HOME>/Resources/fdtd-library: 129 items (96 Structures + 33 Analysis). The MCP tools library_list / library_insert wrap this command
An unknown id is silently ignored by the engine, so validate against the catalog first (engine/library.py: find/suggest)
